62	## Sub-dependencies with `yield` { #sub-dependencies-with-yield }
    63	
    64	You can have sub-dependencies and "trees" of sub-dependencies of any size and shape, and any or all of them can use `yield`.
    65	
    66	**FastAPI** will make sure that the "exit code" in each dependency with `yield` is run in the correct order.
    67	
    68	For example, `dependency_c` can have a dependency on `dependency_b`, and `dependency_b` on `dependency_a`:
    69	
    70	{* ../../docs_src/dependencies/tutorial008_an_py310.py hl[6,14,22] *}
    71	
    72	And all of them can use `yield`.
    73	
    74	In this case `dependency_c`, to execute its exit code, needs the value from `dependency_b` (here named `dep_b`) to still be available.
    75	
    76	And, in turn, `dependency_b` needs the value from `dependency_a` (here named `dep_a`) to be available for its exit code.
    77	
    78	{* ../../docs_src/dependencies/tutorial008_an_py310.py hl[18:19,26:27] *}
    79	
    80	The same way, you could have some dependencies with `yield` and some other dependencies with `return`, and have some of those depend on some of the others.
    81	
    82	And you could have a single dependency that requires several other dependencies with `yield`, etc.
    83	
    84	You can have any combinations of dependencies that you want.
    85	
    86	**FastAPI** will make sure everything is run in the correct order.
    87	
    88	/// note | Technical Details
    89	
    90	This works thanks to Python's [Context Managers](https://docs.python.org/3/library/contextlib.html).
    91	
    92	**FastAPI** uses them internally to achieve this.
    93	
    94	///

content.text: The documentation example with three interdependent `yield` dependencies (`dependency_c` depending on `dependency_b`, which depends on `dependency_a`) is in the **"Sub-dependencies with `yield`"** section of `docs/en/docs/tutorial/dependencies/dependencies-with-yield.md` (lines 62–94). It references the code sample file `docs_src/dependencies/tutorial008_an_py310.py`, which defines `dependency_a`, `dependency_b`, and `dependency_c` as chained yield-based dependencies.
